story.title: Deadly Earthquake Strikes Colombia, Causing Widespread Destruction
story.summary: A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, resulting in at least 132 fatalities and over 570 injuries. The quake, described as the country's strongest in years, led to significant destruction, with many buildings collapsing and rescue efforts underway to find survivors. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency shortly after taking office, and the European Union is providing support for rescue operations.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the rescue effort so difficult?
explore_lenses.title: Remote terrain and urban collapses slow searches
explore_lenses.summary: The response must cover damaged cities as well as the remote Chocó area near the epicenter. Communications and transport constraints may delay confirmation of casualties and delivery of rescue resources.

claims.text: San José del Palmar, near the epicenter, is in mountainous Chocó; it has no airport, while parts of the regional capital Quibdó lost phone service after the quake.
AP reported that much of Chocó is reachable only by boat or plane, which can complicate assessment of damage and casualties outside the main cities.
The quake damaged or destroyed hundreds of buildings across Cali, Pereira, Quibdó and Manizales, leaving rescue teams to search multiple urban sites rather than a single impact zone.

explore_lenses.label: What does the emergency declaration change?
explore_lenses.title: It concentrates response authority and funding
explore_lenses.summary: The national emergency declaration is intended to speed recovery financing, while the government coordinates the immediate response through the national disaster-management system. Local authorities have also imposed short-term restrictions to protect relief operations.

claims.text: President Abelardo de la Espriella declared an emergency to expedite funding for earthquake recovery, according to AP.
The president suspended planned travel and convened a Unified Command Post at the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management, as well as the National Disaster Management Committee.
Mayors Mauricio Salazar of Pereira and Alejandro Eder of Cali said their curfews were meant to prevent looting and facilitate relief work.
The European Commission has mobilized Copernicus satellite services to support rescue operations, according to Euronews.

explore_lenses.label: What dangers remain after the main quake?
explore_lenses.title: Aftershocks and incomplete damage assessments
explore_lenses.summary: Rescue and safety decisions now depend on aftershock monitoring and inspections of buildings, hospitals, transport links and airports. The official casualty count may continue to change as authorities reach affected areas and reconcile reports.

claims.text: The Colombian Geological Service described the quake as Colombia’s strongest recorded in the 21st century and reported that it was followed by several aftershocks.
Forecast: the Colombian Geological Service said further aftershocks are probable; by 18:30 local time on August 11 it had recorded 47.
Authorities suspended flights at six airports while assessing damage, and hospitals in five cities were placed on red alert.
The reported death toll had risen from 132 to 169 by August 11, while the government had not published a new national tally since the prior day, illustrating that casualty reporting remained fluid.

story_report.summary: A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, killing at least 132 people and injuring more than 570, while rescue crews searched damaged buildings for survivors. President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency to speed recovery funding as authorities confronted widespread destruction across several cities. The Colombian Geological Service described the quake as the country’s strongest recorded in the 21st century; it was followed by aftershocks, with further tremors considered probable.

sections.heading: Remote Chocó Complicates Damage Assessment
sections.body: Near the epicenter, San José del Palmar is in mountainous Chocó and has no airport, while parts of the regional capital, Quibdó, lost phone service after the quake. Much of Chocó can be reached only by boat or plane, complicating assessments beyond major cities. Hundreds of buildings were damaged or destroyed across Cali, Pereira, Quibdó and Manizales, requiring rescue teams to work at multiple urban sites.

sections.heading: Emergency Response Expands Across Colombia
sections.body: De la Espriella suspended planned travel and convened a Unified Command Post at the National Unit for Disaster Risk Management and the National Disaster Management Committee. Authorities suspended flights at six airports while damage was assessed, and hospitals in five cities were placed on red alert. The mayors of Pereira and Cali said curfews were intended to prevent looting and help relief operations; the European Commission mobilized Copernicus satellite services for rescue support.

unresolved.text: The extent of damage and the number of people trapped in remote parts of Chocó had not been established.
Casualty reporting remained fluid: reports said the death toll had risen from 132 to 169 by August 11, but the government had not published a new national tally since the previous day.

It remained unclear how many damaged buildings were unsafe, how long transport disruptions would last, whether more victims would be found, and how emergency recovery funds would be allocated or when they would be distributed.

related_stories.title: Syrian Court Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
related_stories.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the country's civil war. The ruling also included their cousin Atef Najib, who was present at the trial. The court's decision follows a lengthy conflict that has resulted in approximately half a million deaths.

related_stories.title: Death Toll Rises to 220 Following 7.4 Magnitude Earthquake in Colombia
related_stories.summary: A 7.4 magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, resulting in at least 220 confirmed deaths and widespread destruction. The epicenter was located near San José del Palmar, approximately 250 miles from Bogotá. Rescue efforts are ongoing, with over 2,700 individuals reported missing as teams race to find survivors in the rubble.

related_stories.title: Trial for Tupac Shakur's Murder Begins Nearly 30 Years Later
related_stories.summary: The trial of Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, accused of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, has commenced in Las Vegas. Jury selection began this week, nearly three decades after Shakur was fatally shot in a drive-by incident. Davis, who has pleaded not guilty, faces a potential life sentence without parole if convicted.

related_stories.title: Thai Prime Minister Suspends Firearm Licences Following School Shooting
related_stories.summary: In response to a recent school shooting, Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has suspended all firearms licences. This decision comes as the bodies of the teenage shooter and his grandparents, whom he killed, were cremated. The Prime Minister also emphasized the need for stricter controls and harsher penalties for firearms-related offenses.
